newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares close easier in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares close easier in active trade.

text.p: Singapore shares ended easier in active trading on Wednesday.
Dealers said there was light buying in selected blue chips and banking stocks but the wider market was still focused on profit taking of Malaysian over-the-counter stocks.
"Banks improved a bit but the action was still on Malaysian issues," said a broker with a local firm.
"The market is a bit directionless and waiting to see what is going to happen on Wall Street," another dealer said.
The key Straits Times Industrial index ended down 6.18 points at 2,220.12. Total market volume was 304 million shares.
The wider market saw 128 counters rising while 239 were easier. "It is not a bad day in terms of volume but the market closed easier mainly on profit taking," said a broker.
Topping the actives was newly listed Jade Technologies with 35.8 million units traded. The counter closed at S$1.05, a 40 percent premium over its initial offer price of S$0.75.
Top gainers included OCBC foreign, DBS foreign and SPH foreign which gained between 40 to 60 Singapore cents each.
Sembawang Corp, Cerebos Pacific and TACC ended lower.
